entries.title: Bulls coaching vacancy living up to the promise of casting a wide net
entries.summary: <p>Recently hired executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham made it sound like a wide net would be used for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls’</a> coaching search and that is proving to be the case.</p><p>The team has already been rumored to have a list of up-and-comers like San Antonio assistant Sean Sweeney, Minnesota’s Micah Nori, Oklahoma City’s Dave Bliss, former player Jerry Stackhouse, and even an in-house candidate in assistant Wes Unseld Jr. on the radar.</p><p>Miami assistant Chris Quinn is now in the mix, as the Bulls have reportedly received permission to talk to Quinn about the vacancy left when Billy Donovan opted to walk away from the head coaching seat after six seasons.</p><p>Quinn fits the job description that Graham laid out when he was hired, not only having a strong reputation for player development, but it doesn’t hurt that he’s worked under Erik Spoelstra — arguably one of the elite coaches in the league — since 2014.</p><p>Again, this remains a process for Graham, who may have to play the long game in a coaching hire with Bliss and Sweeney still involved in the Western Conference Finals.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Teen sets Kane County Cougars' bus ablaze in Winnipeg
entries.summary: <p>The Kane County Cougars’ bus was set on fire and destroyed early Thursday in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and a 15-year-old girl is facing charges related to arson. No one was hurt.</p><p>The Cougars, who were in town to play the Goldeyes in the American Association of Professional Baseball, were in their hotel when the teen allegedly set fire to the bus, which was engulfed in flames. Police arrived at the scene at around 1:50 a.m., and firefighters extinguished the blaze.</p><p>"Everyone is OK, and we are still determining if any gear or personal property was lost," Cougars vice president and general manager Curtis Haug told CBC News.</p><p>The Goldeyes helped the Cougars procure a bus to take them to Fargo, North Dakota, the next stop on their road trip. Windstar, the company whose bus was destroyed, will send a bus to Fargo to bring the Geneva-based Cougars home.</p><p>"We are very disappointed that this could happen to our family-owned company, and the loss of this vehicle will impact our business and operations," Windstar operations manager Jackson Greteman wrote in an email to CBC News, adding that the bus was worth $425,000.</p><p>"We are happy that no one was hurt in this reckless act of vandalism and are cooperating with local authorities."</p><p>Police at first took two teens into custody. The girl facing charges was released.<br></p>
